title: City descriptor
description: What a city must declare before any of its inputs can be built or run. This is the identity half of the input contract; `required_fields.json` is the value half and `layers.json` is the artefact half. The rule this schema exists to enforce is the repository's oldest hard constraint: a study extent is DERIVED from a boundary dataset and a named selector, never typed in as a rectangle. A typed rectangle cannot be wrong in a way anyone notices - one clipped 87 of 1,500 core SA1s out of the road network and survived three phases.

schema_version.description: Bumped only when this schema changes in a way an existing city descriptor would fail.

id.description: The directory name under cities/ and the value of the city selector environment variable.

name.description: Human name of the modelled region. NOT a suburb of it - naming a five-LGA region after one suburb is how this project acquired a stale codename.

jurisdiction.description: Which country's and which agency's open data the adapters speak. This is what decides whether an adapter can be reused or must be written.

crs.description: The projected CRS every metric layer is expressed in. State the datum: EPSG:28356 is GDA94, and EPSG:7856 is its GDA2020 counterpart - this repository carried the wrong datum label in four documents at once.

seed.description: The one seed everything synthetic derives from. Must equal B.population.seed in the registry.

boundary.description: How the study extent is DERIVED. `selector` names features in `dataset`; it is never a bounding box. `bbox` is deliberately not a property of this schema - if a harvest needs one, it is computed from the resolved boundary at run time and printed so it can be checked.

dataset.description: The boundary dataset the selector resolves against, e.g. an ABS ASGS edition.

level.description: The administrative level the selector names, e.g. LGA.

selector.description: Named features forming the core study area.

external_tier.description: The boundary treatment beyond the core: what is retained, at what zone level, and why. A model with no external tier still declares one, with an empty selector and a stated reason.

zone_system.description: Which zone geography each side of a trip is modelled at.

modes.description: The mode vocabulary. Must match RUN.mode_choice.modes in the registry - a mode named here and absent there reaches nothing.

day_types.description: Day types modelled. Each needs an overlay under overlays/day/.

mode_share_target.description: WHICH GEOGRAPHY the observed mode share refers to, named explicitly. This is a schema property because getting it wrong is silent and inverts a headline: this project holds two mode-share series over different populations, and reading the wrong one flipped a result.

filter_value.description: The literal the observed series is filtered on - the value that appears in the data, not the prose name. The city name was typed into three framework modules as a constant before this field existed.

intervention.description: The thing being tested counterfactually. Optional: a city may be modelled with no intervention at all, as a base only.

mode.description: The transit schedule transportMode the intervention runs as (e.g. tram, rail, bus). The measurement layer attributes intervention patronage by THIS, matched against each boarded route's own scheduled transportMode - never by a name heuristic over line ids.

adapters.description: The acquisition scripts under this city's extract/ directory, and what each one lands. These are jurisdiction-specific BY NATURE - the framework does not pretend otherwise. Paths are city-relative.

sources.description: Every upstream data source and its licence. The licence boundary must stay visible: a share-alike layer merged into a permissive artefact without a note is a licence breach that no test can see.

unobtained.description: Inputs this city could not obtain, each with the reason and the field that sweeps in its place. Declared here so a reader sees the gaps in the same file as the claims - and so `check_city.py` can refuse a city that pins one to a point value.
